toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.methodChoice: Collected two items. X14 (printer job records) showed what each job received, whether it was overridden, and what was printed, across all lines and from before the changes. X1 (ERP shelf-life audit trail) tied the change in the payload to a specific CC-309 entry and identified other products with similar entries.
output.brief:
This is a data problem, not an operator or firmware problem. Printer logs show every Veltranol job printed exactly what the integration service sent, with no overrides. From 4 Oct it sent 36 months' shelf life, not 24. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered an approved 36-month value valid only from 1 Mar 2027; the ERP still shows 24 as current, yet the future value reached the printers. Agency operators and the new firmware gave correct output until 3 Oct; permanent staff on Line 1 were affected too. Operator and camera checks use the same data, so couldn't catch it.

Seventeen Veltranol jobs are affected, including Kestrel's three lots, and the fault was still live on 10 Nov. Two other products had future-dated entries on 20 Oct and may be exposed; there is no packing data yet. I'm highly confident of the cause, less sure where the future value is picked up.

Don't remove agency operators or issue warnings; keep the camera check. Remove the future-dated Veltranol value, hold every Veltranol lot packed since 3 Oct, add a second-person expiry check at each setup, inspect retained cartons of those two products, and have Corvane explain.
